extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent agents and attorneys), USPTO disciplinary readers, and counsel involved in USPTO ethics/discipline matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO (formation of business entities, handling client funds and files, client communication, competence/diligence, recordkeeping), and the types of sanctions/remedies the Office may impose in disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on forming a partnership with a non-practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not form a partnership with a non-practitioner if any of the activities of the partnership consist of the practice of patent, trademark, or other law before the Office (37 C.F.R. § 10.49 for pre-May 3, 2013 activities; 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(b) for on/after May 3, 2013 activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order finds that Mr. Neeser formed 'Inventor Soup' with a non-practitioner for the express purpose of providing patent legal services and non-legal services, and that the partnership's activities included practice before the USPTO. Forming such a partnership is a rules violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit advance legal fees and expenses into a client trust account
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall deposit into a client trust account legal fees and expenses that have been paid in advance, to be withdrawn by the practitioner only as fees are earned or expenses incurred (37 C.F.R. § 11.115(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Neeser received advance payments for patent legal services and did not place those funds in a trust account; he thereby violated § 11.115(c). The rule requires segregation of unearned client funds until earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safekeeping client property; keep client property separate from practitioner property
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must hold property of clients (including unearned legal fees and expenses) in the practitioner's possession separate from the practitioner's own property, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to maintain a trust account satisfying § 11.115(a) results in commingling of client funds with personal funds and constitutes a violation; the order states Mr. Neeser failed to hold client property separate from his own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain required accounting and trust records
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must keep required accounting records for client funds as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.115 (recordkeeping provisions such as § 11.115(f)(1) / related subparagraphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Mr. Neeser did not maintain separate accounts for unearned client funds, he also failed to keep required accounting records, violating the recordkeeping provisions of § 11.115.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act with reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client (37 C.F.R. § 11.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of failure include repeatedly promising and failing to provide drafts, late drafting, missing filing requirements, and not meeting statutory due dates; the order found these failures with respect to Client #1 and Client #2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent handling of matters before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must competently handle matters entrusted to them, including meeting statutory due dates and applying the requisite legal/technical skill (37 C.F.R. § 11.101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order found that incompetence (e.g., failing to include filing fee, inventor's declaration, and proper drawings) resulted in incomplete filings and abandonment of client applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptly comply with reasonable client requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from a client (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order finds Mr. Neeser failed to promptly comply with Client #1's reasonable information requests, contributing to prejudice to the client's rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise clients regarding deadlines and priority/filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must advise clients regarding deadlines for filing and other procedural requirements necessary to protect client rights (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With Client #2, the practitioner failed to advise regarding deadlines for filing a complete U.S. national phase patent application claiming PCT priority, contributing to abandonment and prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry out contract of employment and fulfill promised services
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must carry out the practitioner's contract of employment and perform services promised to the client (cited violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(2) for pre-May 3, 2013 activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order finds Mr. Neeser failed to carry out his contract with Client #2 by not filing a complete national phase application as hired and agreed to do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw properly when representation ends or is terminated
rubrics_metrics.description: When ceasing representation, a practitioner must withdraw in accordance with the applicable rule (37 C.F.R. § 11.116).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes Mr. Neeser did not withdraw representation in accordance with § 11.116 after failing to complete filings, which is a rules violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to Office procedural notices (e.g., Notices of Missing Parts) and complete required filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must respond properly and timely to USPTO procedural notices (such as Notices of Missing Parts) and ensure complete filings to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Neeser received a Notice of Missing Parts for Client #2's national phase application and failed to properly reply, resulting in abandonment; practitioners must timely and correctly address such notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conduct that prejudices clients' intellectual property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner conduct (omissions or acts) must not prejudice clients' IP rights; failures to provide adequate review opportunity, file complete applications, or meet deadlines can constitute prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states Client #1's and Client #2's IP rights were prejudiced by failure to provide opportunity to review drafts, failure to file complete applications, and missing procedural responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remedial obligations upon finding misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose sanctions including suspension from practice, publication of the disciplinary order, limited recognition to facilitate compliance, dissociation from Customer Numbers/PKI certificates, and restrictions on obtaining Customer Numbers until reinstated (various provisions cited: 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26, 11.58, 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the agreed sanction included a 12‑month suspension, compliance with § 11.58, publication in the OED FOIA Reading Room and Official Gazette, 30 days limited recognition to comply with § 11.58(b), dissociation of Customer Numbers and PKI, prohibition on applying for Customer Numbers until reinstated, and that the record can be used in future disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigating/aggravating factors in determining discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office considers mitigating factors (e.g., remorse, lack of prior disciplinary history, cooperation with OED) and may treat prior misconduct as aggravating in future proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order lists Mr. Neeser's remorse, no prior disciplinary history, and full cooperation as mitigating factors. It also states the record may be considered in future proceedings as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement/disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties may agree on allocation of costs; in this matter each party shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement provides that the OED Director and Practitioner each bear their own costs.
